chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'I came to the Imam, and he had preceded me by one rak'ah during the Fajr prayer. So when he offered the Taslim, it occurred to me in my heart that I had completed [the prayer]. So I did not cease to remember Allah until the sun rose. So when it rose, I stood up and remembered that the Imam had preceded me by one rak'ah.' He said, 'If you were in your place, then complete with one rak'ah, and if you had already departed, then upon you is the repetition [of the prayer].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I missed a rak'ah with the Imam after the prayer has ended?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between remaining in a state of prayer (maqam) versus having fully concluded it (inṣaraf) when joining the Imam late. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the continuity of congregational prayer, where the validity of the follower's portion depends on their physical and spiritual presence relative to the Imam's final salams. This ruling ensures that the congregational aspect (jamāʿah) is preserved even when timing discrepancies occur.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said, ‘I went over to the Imam and he was ahead of me by one Rak’at during Al-Fajr. So when he offered Salām, it occurred in my heart that I had completed. So I did not cease to mentioned Allahazwj until the sun emerged. So when the sun emerged, I got up and I remembered that the Imam had preceded me by one Rak’at’. So heasws said: ‘If you were in your place, so complete with one Rak’at, and if you had left, so upon you is the repeating’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali al-Nu‘man from al-Flusayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I come to the Imam when he is one Rak‘at ahead of me in the morning Salah (prayer). When he says Sal am (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) I, thinking to have completed, remain speaking of Allah until sunrise. At sunrise I stood up and remembered that the Imam was one Rak‘at ahead of me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If you are still in your place, complete it with one Rak‘at but if you have moved away, perform your Salah (prayer) again.’”
